note: Score honestly. A generous score helps nobody. Structure inspired by Jake Schincariol's li-profile rubric (MIT), adapted with topic-consistency and bilingual items.

items.full_marks: Who you help + what changes for them + one proof. Uses the pillar vocabulary. Not just the job title. Uses most of the 220 characters.
The ~2 lines before 'see more' name the reader's problem or your position. No 'passionate about', no 'proven track record', no third person.
Second person, one or two real numbers, what you do, what to contact you for. Under 1,400 characters. Passes ink score.
Headline, About and current role all use the same 3-5 pillar terms your posts use (360Brew topic matching).
One line of scope then 2-3 outcome bullets with numbers that are allowed to be public. Duties don't count as outcomes.
Three items: best post, one proof asset (talk, article, case), one way to contact you.
Last two roles detailed; roles older than 10 years compressed to one line.
Recent, face ~60% of frame, eyes visible, plain background.
One positioning line + one way to reach you. Not the default, not a stock skyline.
At least 1 original post per week in the last 8 weeks, in your pillars. Reposts and certification shares don't count.
Bilingual profile set up (FR/EN secondary language) if you post in both.
Top 3 skills match pillars; at least 2 recommendations from the last 3 years.
